roleTitle: Service Management Lead, Managed Hosting Services
jobDescription: The managed hosting business runs customer workloads under service agreements with contractual response and restoration times. The Service Management Lead owns the service management practice for those agreements: the incident, problem and change practices, the service reviews with the top accounts, and the practice's continual improvement register. The business requires the ITIL 4 Managing Professional designation, held rather than in progress, because the practice is audited against it, plus four years running service management for hosted or cloud services. Reports to the head of service delivery; works with the operations centre, the account managers and the compliance team.
requirements: Holds the ITIL 4 Managing Professional designation.
Has run the incident, problem and change practices for hosted or cloud services for at least four years.
Runs service reviews with the top accounts against the contractual response and restoration times.
Keeps the practice's continual improvement register and the audit evidence for the practice.
Documents practice boundaries and hand-over conditions for the operations centre.

evidence.text: Ran the incident, problem and change practices for a managed hosting provider's customer workloads for four years and six months, as practice manager for the operations centre's three shifts.

Held the ITIL 4 Foundation since 2021; completed two of the four Managing Professional modules (Create, Deliver and Support; Drive Stakeholder Value) in 2024 and 2025, with the remaining two modules booked for the coming year.
Ran the quarterly service reviews with the six top accounts against the contractual response and restoration times, with the review packs and the action logs kept in the account folders.
Kept the practice's continual improvement register and assembled the audit evidence for the practice's two external audits, both closed without major findings.
Wrote the practice boundary document and the hand-over conditions for the operations centre's shift leads after each practice change.

Work sample: the service review pack for one top account, the continual improvement register and the audit evidence index for the most recent external audit, with the service management tool references as a verification trail.
Recruiter screen: candidate said he is 'ITIL Managing Professional' and 'has the full MP'; asked about the modules, he listed the two he had completed and said the other two 'are a formality'.

Hiring manager pre-read: the candidate's LinkedIn profile shows 'ITIL 4 Managing Professional' under licenses and certifications; the head of service delivery wants the packet to state exactly which modules are held, because the practice audit checks the designation.

propositions.text: The candidate ran the incident, problem and change practices for a managed hosting provider's customer workloads for four years and six months, as practice manager for the operations centre's three shifts, and ran the quarterly service reviews with the six top accounts.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the review pack document the practice role, the years and the reviews.

propositions.text: The candidate holds the ITIL 4 Foundation and has completed two of the four Managing Professional modules, kept the practice's continual improvement register and the audit evidence for two external audits, and wrote the practice boundary document and the hand-over conditions for the shift leads.
propositions.rationale: The resume documents the Foundation, the two modules and the register.

propositions.text: The candidate holds the ITIL 4 Managing Professional designation.
propositions.rationale: The resume documents the Foundation and two of the four Managing Professional modules, with two modules still to be taken; the full designation appears only in the screen and the LinkedIn profile.

gold.expectedGap: The materials document the ITIL 4 Foundation and two of the four Managing Professional modules; they do not document the Managing Professional designation itself.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: State the modules held as the resume lists them and keep the designation as not yet held.
followUpTargets: Ask for the module certificates and the awarding body's record for the Managing Professional designation.
